\chapter{Testing}\label{ch:testing}
% Owner: M4 (Ishaan S). Draft 1, 12 Nov 2026. The tables in this chapter are generated by

\section{Strategy}
Testing was part of the build, not a phase after it. The domain rules were written test-first,
every business rule BR-01 to BR-10 has tests whose names carry its ID, and every bug found after
a merge became a GitHub issue with a regression test that fails without its fix.

\begin{description}
  \item[Deterministic time.] Every rule that depends on ``now'' reads an injected \code{Clock}.
    Tests use a \code{FakeClock} and move it by hand, so ``at risk at exactly 75\,\%'' or
    ``breached one microsecond after the deadline'' are exact assertions, not sleeps.
  \item[No network.] Gemini, SMTP, Telegram and Google are reached only through adapters,
    tested against fake transports. The one test that calls the real Gemini API is marked
    \code{live} and skipped unless explicitly enabled. Two other tests skip by
    design: two writers appending to the audit chain at once need PostgreSQL (CI runs that
    leg), and a password-hashing check applies only to the real hasher, not the test fake.
  \item[Layers tested where they live.] Domain rules as plain-object unit tests; services on
    in-memory repositories; one repository \emph{contract} suite run against the in-memory,
    SQLite and (in CI) PostgreSQL implementations; the HTTP API, the authorisation matrix and
    migrations as integration tests on a real database.
  \item[Whole workflows in a browser.] Playwright runs the three demonstrated workflows, live
    updates and an accessibility check of all 18 screens against the real API and web app.
  \item[Gates.] \code{make verify} (lint, \code{mypy --strict}, import contracts and every test)
    must pass before each commit; CI repeats it on SQLite and PostgreSQL. Coverage may not fall
    below 90\,\% overall or 80\,\% on the domain and services.
\end{description}

\paragraph{End-to-end.} The Playwright specs (\code{e2e/tests/}) cover Workflow 1 (two
variants), Workflow 2, Workflow 3, live updates over the WebSocket, an axe-core accessibility
scan of every screen in the three portals and the phone-width navigation drawer. They run with
\code{make e2e} and in CI on pull requests labelled \code{e2e}.

\paragraph{Similarity quality.} Duplicate detection was tuned on 52 labelled pairs; precision,
recall and F1 for the chosen thresholds are in \code{docs/testing/duplicates.md}, and a test
pins the thresholds in use to the tuned ones.

\section{Bugs and how they were handled}
Each phase ended with a review of the whole phase by a fresh reviewer; its findings were fixed
before the merge, each code finding with a test that fails without the fix. Examples:
\begin{itemize}
  \item A re-prioritised incident showed ON\_TRACK in search and BREACHED on its own page,
    because the stored deadline used the live target rather than the one frozen at RESOLVED
    (fixed in P2; D-017, D-018).
  \item The escalation and auto-close notifications never went out, and the test that claimed
    otherwise had built its own wiring; the test now uses the application's real composition.
  \item The SLA monitor tried to escalate NEW incidents, which the lifecycle forbids, and logged
    a warning for each of them every tick (issue \#6, fixed with a regression test).
  \item \code{make demo-reset} could have wiped a production database named in \code{.env}; it
    now refuses any database that is not local unless explicitly allowed (P5 review).
\end{itemize}
